book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

parts.note: surface reading: something lubricated to an unusual degree, like a machine
setter's reading: in the manner of a peer, someone who is not a commoner, and 'well-oiled' is slang for very drunk

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is DRUNK AS A LORD. 'Uncommonly' is read as 'not like a commoner', pointing to a member of the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means extremely intoxicated, and well-oiled is British slang for tipsy, so the uncommon drinker is a peer.

clue.text: Varying tones are to vibrate sympathetically

indicators.note: varying things change form, so these letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Different musical notes set things humming in sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' does double service: it is part of the letters to shuffle, so only 'to' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To resonate is for a body to vibrate in response to a matching frequency, which is sympathetic vibration.

parts.note: surface reading: feeling disoriented or bewildered
setter's reading: the sense of touch has been lost

explanation.walkthrough: 'Feeling' is a noun here, sensation, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Numb describes a body part deprived of sensation, so it is the state where physical feeling has gone.

parts.note: surface reading: a cold, fickle person
setter's reading: a creature that flies, from icy northern regions

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty' usually means capricious; here it means given to flight, a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird breeds in the frozen far north, hence frigid, and is famous for its very long migratory flights.

clue.text: Expose to air for a time in Atomic Energy Research Establishment

indicators.note: in places the pieces before it inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: the initials of the former British nuclear research centre at Harwell
taken as written
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Something is left out in the open for a while at a nuclear research site.
explanation.definitionFit: To aerate is to let air into or through something, such as soil or a liquid, which is exposing it to air.

parts.note: surface reading: what happens to an acorn, as if asking its fate
setter's reading: what the seed grows into

explanation.walkthrough: The question sounds like it is about an acorn's fate (eaten, buried by a squirrel); it simply asks what it grows into.
explanation.definitionFit: An acorn is the seed of the oak, so given time it matures into that tree.

clue.text: Straight talking, it is not reported

definitions.meaning: first meaning: speaking plainly and frankly
second meaning: the grammar term for quoting words as spoken, as opposed to reported speech

explanation.surface: Frank talk that never makes it into the news.
explanation.walkthrough: Grammar distinguishes direct speech ('I'm tired') from reported or indirect speech (she said she was tired).
explanation.definitionFit: Read loosely the phrase means frank talk, and in grammar it is quotation of actual words rather than a reported version.

indicators.note: something rife runs riot and spreads unchecked, so the letters before it are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about where pornography circulates freely.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: contraband is notoriously rife in jails.
explanation.definitionFit: A jail is a place where contraband such as pornographic material is commonly said to circulate, so the question describes it.

clue.text: Lover who is the reverse of tender

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word written back to front

parts.note: tender as in painful to the touch

explanation.surface: A lover who is anything but gentle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse of tender' looks like it means rough or harsh, but it is read literally: a synonym of tender, turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of erotic love, so he stands for a lover by personification.

clue.text: Scandalmonger heaps dirt on gardener perhaps

indicators.note: one thing heaped on another is placed in front of it, so the first piece leads

parts.note: muck is dirt or filth
one who rakes, as a gardener does; 'perhaps' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A gossip flings dirt over someone tending the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A muckraker digs up and spreads scandal about others, the same role as a scandalmonger, so they are synonyms.

parts.note: surface reading: the official song of a nation
setter's reading: nation means country, and an anthem is a piece of music

explanation.walkthrough: Swap each word for a synonym: national becomes country, anthem becomes music, giving a genre rather than a state song.
explanation.definitionFit: Country is a synonym for nation, so the genre name is a literal rewording of the question.

clue.text: Performing well less than one hymn

indicators.note: less than a whole word means it falls short by a letter at its end

parts.note: the word one with its final letter removed
a hymn is a religious song

explanation.surface: A singer hitting form needs barely a single hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less than one' looks like a quantity; it means the word one cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: On song is British idiom for being in top form, especially of a sportsperson or performer having a good day.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: renowned, important in history
second meaning: belonging to the past

explanation.surface: Someone once celebrated who has faded from view.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic means notable enough to be remembered, and in grammar or loose use it also describes things of past times rather than now.

clue.text: Novelist's turn to include distant transportation company

indicators.note: to include something is to take it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: H. G. Wells, author of The Time Machine
a go is a turn in a game
far means distant

explanation.surface: A writer's chance to take a far-off haulage firm on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Wells Fargo ran stagecoaches and express freight in the American West before becoming a bank, so it was a transport company.

clue.text: Not quite in position to make a score

definitions.text: Not quite in position to make a score

parts.note: surface reading: a player or team just short of scoring a goal or point
setter's reading: a score is twenty, so the place one short of it is the ordinal just before twentieth

explanation.walkthrough: A score is the old word for twenty; the answer is the position immediately before the twentieth.
explanation.definitionFit: Nineteenth is the ordinal place one short of twentieth, so it is literally not quite at the score position.

indicators.note: to have held something is to enclose it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Les is the usual short form of the name Lesley
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Lesley gripped a fresh piece of optical kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens bends light passing through it, and that bending is refraction, so it is a refracting device by definition.

parts.note: a cricket side that is batting is in
a charge is a rush forward to attack

explanation.surface: Someone accountable for an aggressive batting display.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting side is 'in' and the fielding side 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in charge means having authority and accountability, so it means responsible as an adjective.

indicators.note: sounding tells us to go by how a word is pronounced, not how it is spelt

parts.note: correct means right, which is pronounced the same as the answer

explanation.surface: A ceremony that sounds properly done.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a formal ceremonial act of worship, which is a religious observance.

clue.text: Laborious effort of a few inside track

indicators.note: inside places the pieces before it within the word for track

parts.note: a trail is a track or path
taken as written
V is the Roman numeral five, taken here as a small number

explanation.surface: Hard toil for a small band working inside a path.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'few' as V (the Roman five) is loose; nothing else in the clue supplies that letter, but the definition and the rest of the build are exact.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is painful or exhausting labour, a literary word for hard work.

clue.text: Coming from Italian city let inferno rage

indicators.note: to rage is to storm about wildly, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone from a Tuscan city allowing a blaze to roar, with a nod to Dante's Inferno.
explanation.walkthrough: Dante, author of the Inferno, came from this city, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Florentine means native to or originating in Florence, the Italian city, so it is an adjective of origin.

indicators.note: of here means made from: the answer is fashioned out of the next word's letters, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something revived after lying neglected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' does double duty: it ends the definition and also tells you the letters that follow come out of order.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to publish or release, so something brought out as a stamp or book has been issued.

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
the suffix that makes a word feminine, as in lioness

explanation.surface: Pricing a jenny for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'female' gives the feminine ending -ESS, placed after the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to judge the worth or amount of something, which is estimating its value.

parts.note: surface reading: a joint in the body, a carpentry joint or a cannabis cigarette
setter's reading: a joint of meat, and the ventilated cupboard that keeps it

explanation.walkthrough: A joint is a roasting cut of meat; a meat safe is a gauze-fronted cupboard for keeping food before refrigerators.
explanation.definitionFit: The cupboard exists to store cuts of meat such as a Sunday roast, so it literally holds the joint.

clue.text: Did not finish school subject — medicine

indicators.note: a word that did not finish stops before its last letter

parts.note: physics is a subject taught at school

explanation.surface: A pupil dropped out of a science course to study medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Physic is an old word for medicine or the medical art, still seen in phrases like physic garden.

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: lime is spread on soil to improve it

explanation.surface: A gardener digging in soil improver.
explanation.definitionFit: Emil is a man's given name, and crosswords use 'man' for any male forename.

parts.note: surface reading: a trap that is instrumental, i.e. key to catching someone
setter's reading: a trap is a snare, and here it is the musical instrument of that name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrumental' means a musical instrument, and drummers also call their kit the traps.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare is a trap for animals, and the snare drum is the percussion instrument named after the wires stretched across it.

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the following words, running across them

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A grounded passenger in bad health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-flier' sounds like someone not taking a plane; it is a flightless bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large South American bird that cannot fly, so it is a non-flier.

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a shoulder joint that is cold

explanation.surface: A snub delivered by a frozen-limbed acquaintance.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the cold shoulder is to snub them, and read literally it is an icy body joint.
